reason: Both quotes, under the ABAC advantages over RBAC, state no policy update is needed for new resources and that fewer policies are created because different policies per job function are not needed.
SEC03-BP02 quote recommends ABAC only when principals and resources are owned by your AWS Organization and gives the external same-tag reason.
Quote contrasts RBAC policies for specific resources with ABAC allowing actions on all resources when the resource tag matches the principal tag.
Quote states continuous monitoring of supported resource types and a finding for resources that allow public or cross-account access.

Quotes state custom policy checks validate against your specified security standards, check new access versus the existing version, and through CLI and API also check that critical actions are not allowed.
FAQ quote calls custom policy checks a paid feature; the policy-validation note states a charge is associated with each check for new access.
Quote states logic-based reasoning on resource-based policies and a finding for each instance of a resource shared outside the account.
Important note states external access analysis covers only resources in the Region where it is enabled and an external access analyzer is needed in each Region with supported resources.

Second quote had empty context, so I checked the snapshot (what-is-access-analyzer lines 35-50): both quotes are one continuous bulleted list under 'analyzes the following resource types for external access', and it matches the claim's 15 types.
Decision-guide quote states set, verify, and refine permissions, analysis of external, internal and unused access, and validation against specified security standards.
Quote states CloudTrail logs are analyzed for actions and services used by a user or role in a date range and a policy is generated from that activity.
Quota row 'Policy generation AWS CloudTrail time range' has default 90 days and maximum 90 days, so it cannot be raised.
Quotes state validation against policy grammar and AWS best practices and findings of security warnings, errors, general warnings and suggestions.
Quote states more than 100 policy checks with actionable recommendations; context ties them to the IAM policy language and best practices.
Quota row gives 1,000 access previews per analyzer per hour as both default and maximum.
Quota row gives 1 account-level analyzer per analyzer type per account per Region, default and maximum both 1.
Quota row gives default 100 archive rules per analyzer with up to 20 values per criterion and maximum 1,000 marked with the Service Quotas footnote.
The row supports a concurrent policy generations quota of 1 (default and maximum), but neither the row nor the page intro states the per-what; the scope 'per account' is not in the quote.
Quota row gives default 5 organization-level external or unused analyzers per type per account per Region, maximum 20 with the configurable-quota footnote.
Quota row gives 1 organization-level internal access analyzer per organization per Region, default and maximum both 1.
Quota row 'Policy generation AWS CloudTrail data size' gives 25 GB default and maximum.
Quote states security warnings are generated when a statement allows access considered overly permissive, in the context of Access Analyzer policy validation.
Quote lists external, internal and unused access analyzers with the purposes stated in the claim.
Quote states continuous monitoring of IAM roles and users, findings for unused roles, unused IAM user access keys and passwords, and unused services and actions for active entities.
FAQ quotes state the unused access analyzer is a paid feature and you pay per IAM role or IAM user analyzed per month.
Quote states unused access findings do not change by Region and an analyzer in each Region is not required; second quote adds that each Regional analyzer is charged.
Quote and context state only permissions existing for the entire tracking period are evaluated, the 90-day example, and a value between 1 and 365 days.
Quotes give the four finding types and state console findings appear for managed policies and inline user or role policies but not inline group policies.
Quote states the analyzer is created for the organization or account, which is the zone of trust, and access by principals within it is considered trusted.

Quotes give the explicit-deny phrase with optional policy ARN, the implicit-deny phrase, and that only one policy type is named when several deny; scope keeps the services-that-support-the-format note.
Quote states AKIA keys are long-term for an IAM user or root user and ASIA keys are temporary credentials created with AWS STS.
Quote states the secret is retrievable only at creation and a lost secret requires deleting the key and creating a new one.

Quotes support a maximum of two access keys per user and creating a second key while the first is active; the causal 'which is what allows rotation' and the step 'then retire the first' are not in the quotes or their context.
Quotes state access keys are long-term credentials for an IAM user or root user and the best practice is temporary credentials such as IAM roles instead.
Quotes state account access manager assigns existing IAM roles to Identity Center users and groups of an organization instance and works alongside permission sets or on its own.
Quota row gives 20 groups per IAM role by default with 'Can be increased: Yes'.
Quote states role sessions assigned by account access manager use the default 1-hour duration regardless of the role's maximum session duration.
Quote and context state ACLs control access by principals in other accounts, are the only non-JSON policy type, and cannot grant permissions within the same account.
Three quotes state the role's permissions do not add to the user's, the original permissions are temporarily given up, not cumulative, and restored on exit.

Quotes state adding an account to the trust policy is only half the trust, by default no users in the trusted account can assume the role, and the admin attaches a policy allowing sts:AssumeRole with the role ARN as Resource.
